column1: # Malayalam's chat suffixes: clitics, auxiliaries and case endings that chat glues onto words
# (സുഖമാണോ, കഴിച്ചോ, വരുന്നുണ്ടോ). The engine reads a typed Latin word with no whole-form match
# as a stem plus one or two of these (engine/core/src/suffix.rs). Small and explicit: every row
# is a guess about words the engine has never seen, so each must be common.
#   latin   the ways people type it, comma-separated, matched against the end of the typed word
#   join    how it fuses with its stem (the mlym plug-in's joins, suffix.rs `Join`):
#           vowel      starts with a vowel: the vowel becomes a sign on the stem (ആണോ, ഉണ്ട്)
#           case       a vowel-initial case ending; as vowel, but not after a stem in ം (ഇൽ)
#           consonant  starts with a consonant; appended after a vowel, ർ or ൾ (ക്ക്)
#           oblique    the oblique ending of a stem in ം, which it replaces (ത്തിൽ)
#   inner   optional: "inner" if another suffix may follow it (വരുന്നു + ഉണ്ട് + ഓ)
# Row order matters: among cuts of equal length, earlier rows and spellings are tried first.
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are skipped.
